quotes.text: Feeding yourself well is one of the simplest ways to say you matter.
You are allowed to take up space at the table, and to nourish yourself while you are there.
Speak to yourself about food the way you would to a friend who is trying.
A rough day of eating is not a moral failure. It is a data point.
Change built on shame does not last. Change built on care does.
You do not have to punish yourself into good habits. Encouragement works better and feels nicer.
Be as patient with your body as you would be with someone you love.
Eating well is an act of respect, not an act of control.
The kindest thing you can do for a tired body is feed it properly and let it rest.
Nobody is fixed by a scolding. Everyone is helped by a good meal and a kind word.
Progress is built on the days you were kind to yourself and tried again.
You are not bad for eating something you enjoy. You are a person with a Tuesday.
Treat your body as a home, not a project. Homes need care, not criticism.
Show up for yourself the way you show up for others: with warmth, consistency and a meal.
Every time you choose to nourish yourself, you are telling yourself you are worth it.
Self-care is not a spa day. Sometimes it is a hot meal and an early night.
Whatever yesterday looked like, today’s meal is a fresh chance to be kind to yourself.
There is no failing at this. There is only learning what works for you, one meal at a time.
You are trying, and trying counts. Log the meal and move on.
Being gentle is not the same as being lazy. It is what makes it possible to keep going.
When you look after your body, you look after the person a lot of people depend on. That is you.
A body that feels cared for tends to be easier to live with.
Some days the kind choice is a salad. Some days it is a slice of cake and a good book. Both can be love.
Do not wait to feel worthy of a good meal. Eat the good meal and feel worthy afterwards.
Encourage yourself the way a good coach would: honest about the plan, warm about the person.
Compare yourself only to yesterday’s you, and only to notice how far you have come.
Cook something for yourself tonight, even if it is small. It says you are worth the trouble.
Everybody has off days. What matters is the next meal, and how kindly you approach it.
Give your body the courtesy you give a guest: something warm, something good, no comments.
It is hard to grow while you are being hard on yourself.
You are doing better than you think. Keep going, gently.
Your worth is not on the scale, in your calorie count or on your plate.
Looking after yourself is not selfish. It is how you get to keep looking after everyone else.
Treat every meal as a small gift to someone you love. Then remember that someone is you.
There is enough time for a proper meal and enough grace for the ones that are not.
Set the bar where you can clear it, and then celebrate clearing it.
If you would not say it to a friend, do not say it to yourself about your plate.
You are not behind. You are exactly where your next good meal can start.
Care for yourself the way you would for someone you have promised to look after.
Softness and discipline are not opposites. The best routines have both.
A missed day is not a broken streak. It is a day, and the next one is waiting.
Lower the standard for what counts as a win. Ate lunch? Win.
Your body has carried you through every hard day you have ever had. It deserves gentle treatment.
Give yourself the credit for the meals you cooked, the water you drank and the walk you took. Nobody else is counting.
Be the person who makes it a little easier for you to eat well tomorrow.
Being hard on yourself is not a plan. A good breakfast is.
It is okay to have a day that was just about getting through. Feed yourself and go to bed.
You can start again at any time, without an apology.
Do not let a lapse become a story about who you are. It is only a meal.
Cheer for the small things. They are the ones that add up.
